observations.note: I am choosing the experiment that will separate the most remaining models on average.

Compared with observation 1, this proposed experiment changes only water. It tests whether adding water changes growth from 50 at fixed mineral, light, and temperature, distinguishing a water benefit in this setting from no benefit. Mineral and light interactions would remain unresolved and require later controlled comparisons. This experiment has not been executed.

Compared with observation 2, this proposal changes only the mineral (none to basalt) with water present, amber light and warm temperature fixed. It tests whether mineral composition changes growth, survival or energy when water is available, i.e. whether water's null effect so far reflects a missing mineral co-factor. A later dry basalt run would be needed to separate a mineral main effect from a water-by-mineral interaction. Light remains untested. Not yet executed.

Verified IMD decision applied (ec8cebff-9a12-42af-9bdf-70313db2be36; artifact SHA-256 a832e2611353d3cb8e8c29d5c6250fe591b58be650413f03a48eb6fe7c746fc9). Hypothesis assessment: Public observation 1 reports growth 50, survival false, and energy 40 without water, with no mineral, under amber light at warm temperature. With only this observation, evidence is insufficient to establish a water benefit or dependence on minerals or light. A water-only contrast can test its effect in this setting, but cannot establish whether that effect changes across mineral or light conditions.

Experiment 3: the plant did not survive, growth 50/100. Spent 2 credits.

Verified IMD decision applied (2cc81d6b-b96b-44ae-8bd2-0c0261d91cfa; artifact SHA-256 731fae9ec1ce1354d832c15b259e028fd1e6910aba1b3f0e043666df4249ac3e). Hypothesis assessment: Facts: observations 1 (no water) and 2 (water), both with no mineral, amber light and warm temperature, gave identical outcomes: growth 50, survived false, energy 40. New comparison: under these fixed conditions, adding water showed no measurable effect, so the public evidence does not support a general water benefit. Inference: any water benefit, if it exists, would have to depend on other factors (mineral, light, or temperature); this single paired contrast cannot rule that out, and outcomes may also have variance not visible from one run each. Unresolved: whether mineral or light changes growth or the water response. The previous assessment (evidence insufficient for a water benefit or for mineral/light dependence) should be revised in one respect: water now shows no effect in the none/amber/warm setting; dependence on mineral and light remains untested and evidence is insufficient.
